# 🌍 Complete Terraform & Infrastructure as Code (IaC) Track

Welcome to your full Terraform learning workspace materialized with **Trak**.

## 📚 Comprehensive Module Index

| Module | Title | Key Topics Covered |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `00-setup-and-iac-foundations` | **IaC & Toolchain** | Declarative vs Imperative, HCL2 syntax, Terraform / OpenTofu CLI |
| `01-hcl-syntax-blocks-and-types` | **HCL Syntax & Types** | Block types (`terraform`, `provider`, `resource`, `data`), data types (`map`, `object`) |
| `02-providers-and-registry` | **Providers & Aliases** | `required_providers`, multi-region provider aliases, Terraform Registry |
| `03-resources-and-dependencies` | **Resources & Graph** | Implicit vs explicit (`depends_on`), `lifecycle` (`create_before_destroy`, `ignore_changes`) |
| `04-variables-outputs-and-locals` | **Variables & Outputs** | `variables.tf`, `terraform.tfvars`, type constraints, custom validations, `sensitive` |
| `05-state-management-and-backends` | **State & S3/DynamoDB** | `terraform.tfstate`, remote backend state locking, `state mv`, `state rm` |
| `06-execution-workflow-and-plan` | **Workflow & Plan** | `init`, `validate`, `fmt`, `plan -out=tfplan`, `apply`, `destroy`, `-target` |
| `07-data-sources-and-remote-state` | **Data Sources** | Reading live cloud infrastructure, `data "terraform_remote_state"` |
| `08-expressions-functions-and-loops` | **Loops & Functions** | `for_each` vs `count`, `for` expressions, `splat` (`*`), `lookup`, `merge`, `try` |
| `09-dynamic-blocks-and-meta-arguments` | **Dynamic Blocks** | `dynamic "ingress" { for_each = ... }`, nested attribute generation |
| `10-modules-reusability-and-composition` | **Modules Architecture**| Root vs Child modules, module inputs/outputs, version pinning |
| `11-workspaces-and-environments` | **Workspaces** | CLI workspaces (`terraform workspace new prod`), directory separation patterns |
| `12-importing-existing-infrastructure` | **Import Blocks** | Terraform 1.5+ declarative `import {}` blocks, reverse engineering code |
| `13-security-and-secret-management` | **Secret Safety** | Vault integration, KMS, AWS Secrets Manager, Checkov/tfsec static scanning |
| `14-policy-as-code-sentinel-opa` | **Policy as Code** | Open Policy Agent (OPA) / Conftest, Sentinel guardrails |
| `15-testing-and-validation-frameworks`| **Native Testing** | Terraform 1.6+ native testing (`.tftest.hcl`), mock providers, assertions |
| `16-production-gitops-and-atlantis` | **GitOps Automation** | Atlantis PR automation, GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline for Terraform |
| `17-interview-questions-and-drills` | **Interview Master Drill** | Top 10 Terraform interview questions, drift detection, state corruption recovery |

---

## 🛠️ Quick Commands

```bash
# Initialize working directory
terraform init

# Review execution plan
terraform plan

# Apply configuration
terraform apply -auto-approve
```

```bash

terraform fmt -recursive

# 2. Validate syntax and internal consistency
terraform validate

# 3. Generate and save deterministic execution plan
terraform plan -out=tfplan

# 4. Apply exact plan file
terraform apply tfplan
```

# 08 - Loops (for_each vs count)

Prefer `for_each` (keyed on distinct string identifiers) over `count` (keyed on numeric array indices) because deleting an item in the middle of a `count` list causes Terraform to destroy and recreate all subsequent resources.

# 17 - High-Yield Terraform Interview Questions 🎯

### Top 5 Interview Questions:
1. **count vs for_each**: `count` relies on integer indices (causing cascading recreations on deletion); `for_each` binds resources to immutable string map keys.
2. **State Locking**: Prevents concurrent runs by acquiring an exclusive lock in DynamoDB before modifying state.
3. **Drift Detection**: `terraform plan` refreshes state against real-world cloud APIs to identify changes made outside Terraform.
4. **Terraform 1.5+ import block**: Allows declarative, version-controlled resource imports and automatic HCL code generation.
5. **Sensitive outputs and state**: `sensitive = true` masks values in CLI logs, but values remain unencrypted in raw `terraform.tfstate` JSON (requiring KMS-encrypted remote backends).

🚀 You have completed the complete Terraform & IaC Mastery track!
